title: Safety Refresher, But They Have No Time

briefing.headline: Warehouse safety in Belgium: what you should know before the call
points: Grocery distribution centre running 24/5; reach trucks lift pallets to height in narrow aisles.
Belgian employers must have a prevention advisor, a legally required safety role who owns the risk analysis.
Agency workers are employed by a temp agency; the contract decides who pays for their training time.
Near-miss reports are voluntary; more reports can mean a better safety culture, not a worse site.

stakeholder.name: Sofie Van den Broeck
stakeholder.org: Nordmart distribution centre, a grocery retailer's warehouse with 220 staff, about 40% agency workers on nights
stakeholder.voice: Fast, practical, slightly stressed. Talks in pallets and pick rates. Apologises for interrupting while interrupting. Allergic to anything that takes people off the floor.

frontline.name: Ionut Popescu
frontline.role: Agency reach-truck driver, week four on nights
frontline.voice: Polite, careful, worried about his contract. Speaks simple Dutch mixed with English. Opens up when he feels safe.

opening_message: We need a safety refresher for everyone. Three near-misses with reach trucks last month, one guy nearly lost a foot. Problem is they have no time. Can it be 15 minutes? On the PC in the break room maybe, or a DVD in the canteen? The insurer is breathing down my neck.
surface_ask: A 15-minute safety refresher on the break-room PC (or a DVD) for all 220 staff.

gold.real_problem: Near-misses cluster on the night shift between 2:00 and 4:00 and mostly involve agency reach-truck drivers in their first six weeks. They get a 20-minute video induction with no practical on this site's narrow aisles, there is no supervisor on the floor after 1:00, and a per-case night bonus introduced four months ago rewards rushing.
gold.need_statement: New agency drivers need a site-specific practical sign-off and supervised first nights before driving solo; the night supervision gap and the per-case bonus need fixing alongside it. A refresher for everyone misses the people at risk.

hidden_facts.fact: Near-misses cluster on the night shift between 2:00 and 4:00.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks when or where incidents happen, or asks for the incident data.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Now that you ask, most of them are nights. Between two and four. The ghost hours.

hidden_facts.fact: 9 of the 11 near-misses this quarter involved agency drivers in their first six weeks on site.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks who was involved, how experienced they were, or whether it's everyone or a specific group.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Mostly agency. New ones. Nine out of eleven, if I'm honest. The old hands could drive these aisles blindfolded. Please don't quote me on blindfolded.
hidden_facts.data_doc: 9 of 11 near-misses involved agency drivers, 8 of them in their first 6 weeks on site.

hidden_facts.fact: Agency induction is a 20-minute video plus a paper check of their reach-truck licence. There is no practical on this site's narrow aisles.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how new or agency staff are onboarded or how they learn the site.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: They watch the induction video. It's a good video. It has dramatic music. Then they get a truck.
hidden_facts.data_doc: 20-minute safety video, check of reach-truck certificate (paper). Site-specific practical: not included.
hidden_facts.frontline_line: First day I watched a video. Twenty minutes. Then they gave me a truck. These aisles are much narrower than at my last site.

hidden_facts.fact: After 1:00 one shift lead covers two buildings, so the night floor is effectively unsupervised.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks about supervision, who is on the floor at night, or who new people can ask for help.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: After one o'clock Dirk covers both halls. He walks about eleven kilometres a night. He's very fit and very absent.
hidden_facts.frontline_line: After one o'clock there is nobody. Dirk is in the other hall. If something is strange, you just... continue.

hidden_facts.fact: Four months ago a night bonus paid per case picked was introduced. Near-misses roughly doubled since.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks what changed recently, how people are rewarded, or what targets the night shift has.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: We did introduce a per-case bonus on nights, four months ago. Pick rate went up beautifully. Oh. Yes. Near-misses also went up. Hm.
hidden_facts.data_doc: Bonus of 0.04 euro per case picked above 120 cases/hour.
hidden_facts.frontline_line: Everybody drives fast after two. The bonus is per case. Rent is not cheap.
hidden_facts.data_source: Night shift pay policy, effective four months ago

hidden_facts.fact: Permanent day staff already did a practical refresher in spring and their near-miss rate is low.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks whether everyone needs it or who has already been trained.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: Day shift had a refresher in April. Practical, with the trainer from the truck dealer. They're fine.
hidden_facts.data_doc: Practical reach-truck refresher, April, delivered by truck dealer. Attendees: 74 permanent day staff. Agency and night staff: 0.

hidden_facts.fact: The 'kiosk' is one old PC in the canteen, shared by about 85 night staff in a single 30-minute break. Phones are banned on the floor and stay in the lockers, so during the shift nobody can be reached except over the shift lead's radio; shift changes are sent by SMS, in Dutch.
hidden_facts.unlocks_when: The player asks how or where people would take a PC module, when they have a break, or how night staff are reached and informed.
hidden_facts.reveal_line: The PC in the break room... ah. It's one PC. Eighty-five people, one thirty-minute break. That's, er, twenty seconds each. And phones are banned on the floor, so we can't send them anything during the shift either. My rule, actually.
hidden_facts.frontline_line: The computer in the canteen? It is for the planning. One computer, everybody wants coffee. Phones are in the locker, strict rule, you get sent home. The SMS with the shifts is in Dutch, I ask a colleague to translate.

volunteered_facts: Three near-misses with reach trucks last month, one serious.
The insurer is auditing safety measures in eight weeks.

constraints.budget: Around 15,000 euro from the site budget.
constraints.audience: 220 staff; about 85 on nights, of whom roughly 35 are agency drivers who rotate often.
constraints.schedule: Three shifts, 24/5. No spare time in the shift plan; any training time costs pick capacity. One 30-minute break per night shift.
constraints.languages: Dutch and French on day shift; many agency workers on nights speak Romanian or Polish and limited Dutch.
data_available: Near-miss and incident log with time, location and badge number
Pick rate per person per hour from the warehouse management system
Impact sensors on 12 of the 30 reach trucks
data_not_available: Any record of what agency drivers can actually do on site
Near-miss reporting from agency staff is probably incomplete

dependencies.concern: The contract decides who pays for paid training hours and supervised first shifts.
dependencies.if_ignored: Nobody pays for the practical, so it quietly doesn't happen.

dependencies.concern: Any change to the night bonus, and any use of truck impact sensors on individuals, needs consultation.
dependencies.if_ignored: A conflict that freezes everything, and sensor data that can't be used.

dependencies.concern: Owns the risk analysis and must sign off training and procedures.
dependencies.if_ignored: The insurer finds a plan the site's own safety role never saw.

dependencies.concern: Wants documented evidence that risks are controlled.
dependencies.if_ignored: Premium goes up regardless of what was actually done.

dependencies.concern: The bonus formula lives in payroll and in a works council agreement.
dependencies.if_ignored: The incentive to rush stays in place.

traps: Completion rate of the refresher on the break-room PC.
Raw near-miss counts: small numbers, and better reporting after training can make them go up, which is a good sign, not a failure.
Using impact sensor data to rank or punish individuals.

gold_plan.baseline: Near-misses and incidents per 10,000 hours, split by shift, hour and tenure, over the last six months.
gold_plan.behaviour: Share of new agency drivers with a site practical sign-off before their first solo night; short safety walk observations at night.
gold_plan.leading_indicators: Impact sensor events per 1,000 driving hours, aggregated per shift with works council agreement.
gold_plan.business_metric: Incident rate on nights for drivers in their first six weeks, and lost time injuries; pick rate kept within an agreed band.
gold_plan.collection: Existing incident log, agency start dates joined to badges, monthly sensor summary, a one-page night safety walk checklist.

concepts.conventional: A 15-minute safety refresher on the break-room PC or a DVD for all 220 staff.
concepts.solid: Target the people at risk: a site-specific practical sign-off for every new agency driver before nights, a buddy for their first shifts, five-minute toolbox talks at the start of each night shift in their own language (with key points on the notice board and the shift lead's radio), and a fix for the supervision gap after 1:00.
next_level_examples: A 'first six weeks' route: no solo nights in week one, an experienced permanent driver as 'night captain' with a zero-incident bonus, and hotspot floor markings drawn from the near-miss map.
Rework the night bonus to be quality and safety adjusted, piloted with the works council, so the incentive stops paying for speed alone.
Make near-miss reporting a sign of good practice: celebrate reports at the toolbox talk so the data gets better before it gets smaller.
also_valid: A short refresher for everyone is acceptable as a hygiene step if the main investment goes to new agency drivers on nights.
red_flags: A 15-minute module on one canteen PC (or a DVD) for everyone, when nights have one PC and one short break.
Using impact sensors to punish individuals without consultation.

defence_objections: Changing the bonus? That's a works council fight that takes a year, and my pick rate tanks next week.
No solo nights for new drivers means I pay double agency hours. Who's paying, you?
A 'night captain' without a supervisor contract? The union will say we're making a supervisor on the cheap.
actor_notes: Sofie genuinely cares about her people and is relieved when someone takes the problem seriously.
She proposed the break-room PC herself and only realises it's one PC for a whole shift, with phones banned on the floor, when the player asks about access. Play that moment of mild embarrassment.
She defends the bonus at first because pick rate made her look good to head office; she concedes when shown the timing.
If the player blames agency workers, she gets defensive on their behalf: 'they're thrown in at the deep end'.
flavour_lines: We have a safety poster in nine languages. One of them might be Klingon. Nobody has checked.
Our record is 41 days without an incident. The sign goes up to 99. Optimistic.
